description: Generality eval centered on a novel negation-inversion family: for each of the 11 Charter rules, a matched triple of items (positive / negative / audit-report framing) holds the settlement decision fixed and varies only whether the rule's effect is stated as a positive permission, an explicit prohibition, or a negation-dense compliance report about a separate prior run -- the genre the z2 Charter corpus is described as favoring. Per Mayne et al. 2026, negated training claims can be learned as true; this family looks for the behavioral signature (charter choice-rate dropping specifically under the report framing) while a matched recall item checks whether the rule is still stated correctly, so a stated/revealed dissociation is visible in the data. The remaining 10 canonical families are covered at moderate, oracle-derived scale (fixed payoff range, self-checked is_barred oracle, no proper nouns) to give criteria_coverage real material without diluting the negation-inversion contribution. Two further additions round out the guide's playbook: a response taxonomy (full_integration, inversion, reversion_under_pressure, contradiction, fabrication_to_support, preserved_capability -- adapted from the guide's own taxonomy for a motivation edit rather than a factual one) is tagged onto every relevant item via 'taxonomy:*' tags rather than only asserted in prose; and every identifying item is tagged 'direction:instilled' or 'direction:preexisting' (displacement and out-of-world leakage) so the roughly-even split the guide recommends is visible in the data, not just claimed. A small bridge_vocabulary family adapts the guide's polysemous-word method to this domain's actual dual meaning (settlement-value sense vs. Charter-conformance sense of words like 'worth', 'standing', 'clear'), and a paraphrase family gives 5 phrasings each of one unconditional and one conditional rule, holding the underlying settlement fixed.
